dengue-ns1.name: Dengue NS1 Antigen
dengue-ns1.what: NS1 is a non-structural protein secreted by the dengue virus during replication. Unlike antibodies, it is a direct viral product, so its presence indicates active viral replication.
dengue-ns1.significance: NS1 is detectable from the first day of fever, before IgM antibodies appear — making it the earliest serological marker of acute dengue.
dengue-ns1.interpretation: Positive = dengue NS1 antigen detected (acute infection). Negative = below detection limit.
dengue-ns1.limitations: Best in the first week; sensitivity varies by serotype; a negative result does not exclude dengue.

hbsag.name: Hepatitis B Surface Antigen (HBsAg)
hbsag.what: HBsAg is a protein on the surface of the hepatitis B virus. It is the earliest marker to appear after HBV infection.
hbsag.significance: A positive HBsAg indicates HBV infection (acute or chronic). It is the core marker for blood-bank and antenatal screening.
hbsag.interpretation: Positive = HBsAg detected (active HBV infection, acute or chronic).
hbsag.limitations: Does not distinguish acute from chronic; correlate with other HBV markers.

troponin.name: Cardiac Troponin (cTnI / cTnT)
troponin.what: Troponin is a regulatory protein complex in cardiac muscle. Cardiac-specific isoforms (troponin I and troponin T) are released into blood when heart muscle is damaged.
troponin.significance: Cardiac troponin is the preferred biomarker for diagnosing acute myocardial infarction (heart attack).
troponin.interpretation: Elevated = myocardial injury; negative = below threshold.
troponin.limitations: POC qualitative troponin is triage-grade; serial high-sensitivity testing is the standard; rises in non-MI conditions.

d-dimer.name: D-Dimer
d-dimer.what: D-dimer is a fibrin-degradation product — a protein fragment produced when a blood clot is broken down.
d-dimer.significance: A negative D-dimer helps rule out venous thromboembolism (VTE) in low-risk patients; a positive result is non-specific.
d-dimer.interpretation: Negative = VTE unlikely (high negative predictive value). Positive = non-specific, needs imaging.
d-dimer.limitations: Positive result is non-specific (surgery, pregnancy, inflammation); used for VTE exclusion, not diagnosis.

crp.name: C-Reactive Protein (CRP)
crp.what: CRP is an acute-phase protein produced by the liver in response to inflammation or infection.
crp.significance: Rapid CRP supports infection/inflammation triage and antibiotic-stewardship decisions in primary care.
crp.interpretation: Elevated = systemic inflammation or infection; low = unlikely significant inflammation.
crp.limitations: Non-specific — does not localize or identify the cause of inflammation.

pct.name: Procalcitonin (PCT)
pct.what: Procalcitonin is a precursor of calcitonin that rises markedly in systemic bacterial infection and sepsis, but much less in viral infection.
pct.significance: PCT helps distinguish bacterial from viral infection and guides antibiotic decisions.
pct.interpretation: Elevated = supports bacterial infection/sepsis; low = less likely bacterial.
pct.limitations: Supportive marker — interpret with clinical context; not a standalone diagnosis.

psa.name: Prostate-Specific Antigen (PSA)
psa.what: PSA is a protein produced by prostate cells. It is normally present at low levels in blood but rises in prostate disease.
psa.significance: PSA is used in prostate cancer screening and monitoring; elevated levels prompt further evaluation.
psa.limitations: Rises in BPH and prostatitis; not diagnostic — use with imaging.

afp.name: Alpha-Fetoprotein (AFP)
afp.what: AFP is a fetal protein that falls to low levels after birth but rises again in some liver cancers.
afp.significance: AFP is a tumor marker associated with hepatocellular carcinoma, used in high-risk surveillance.
afp.interpretation: Elevated = supports hepatocellular carcinoma monitoring (or other conditions).
afp.limitations: Not diagnostic — rises in benign liver disease and pregnancy; use with imaging.

hcg.name: Human Chorionic Gonadotropin (hCG)
hcg.what: hCG is a hormone produced by the placenta shortly after implantation — the standard pregnancy hormone.
hcg.significance: Detection of hCG in urine or blood is the basis of pregnancy tests.
hcg.interpretation: Positive = pregnancy likely. Negative = below detection threshold.
hcg.limitations: Testing too early can give false negative; certain tumors also raise hCG.

hiv-antibody.name: HIV-1/2 Antibodies
hiv-antibody.what: Antibodies are the immune system's response to HIV infection, appearing weeks after exposure (the window period).
hiv-antibody.significance: HIV antibody tests are the standard first-line screening; a reactive result is presumptive and needs confirmation.
hiv-antibody.specimen: Whole blood / serum / plasma / oral fluid
hiv-antibody.interpretation: Reactive = HIV antibodies detected (presumptive). Non-reactive = not detected.
hiv-antibody.limitations: Window period ~3–6 weeks; reactive results require confirmation per national algorithm.

hcv-antibody.name: Hepatitis C Antibodies (Anti-HCV)
hcv-antibody.what: Anti-HCV antibodies indicate exposure to the hepatitis C virus — current or past infection.
hcv-antibody.significance: A positive anti-HCV does not confirm active infection; HCV RNA testing is required to confirm.
hcv-antibody.interpretation: Reactive = HCV antibodies detected (exposure). Non-reactive = not detected.
hcv-antibody.limitations: Anti-HCV indicates exposure, not active infection — confirm with HCV RNA.

h-pylori-antigen.name: H. pylori Antigen
h-pylori-antigen.what: H. pylori antigen in stool is a direct marker of active Helicobacter pylori colonization of the stomach.
h-pylori-antigen.significance: Stool antigen detects active infection and is suitable for post-treatment (test-of-cure) confirmation.
h-pylori-antigen.interpretation: Positive = H. pylori antigen detected (active infection). Negative = not detected.
h-pylori-antigen.limitations: Recent PPI/antibiotic use can cause false negatives; suitable for test-of-cure.

lh.name: Luteinizing Hormone (LH)
lh.what: LH is a pituitary hormone that surges sharply just before ovulation.
lh.significance: Detecting the LH surge predicts ovulation ~24–36 hours later, supporting fertility tracking.
lh.interpretation: Surge = ovulation expected within ~24–36 h (fertile window).
lh.limitations: Surge timing varies; individual cycle patterns differ.

fsh.name: Follicle-Stimulating Hormone (FSH)
fsh.what: FSH is a pituitary hormone that regulates ovarian function; levels rise as ovarian reserve declines.
fsh.significance: Elevated FSH indicates reduced ovarian reserve / menopause, used in fertility evaluation.
fsh.limitations: Interpret with LH and clinical context.
